items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: the road to be Abbey Lincoln’s musical director, and that was another good experience.

ctx.x: No. It was — everything, because you know each was a different experience. Okay now when I was with Max Roach, you know we performed and Max loved to do all these different times. So I understood 5/4 but 7/4 and 13 and all that, that’s a little bit difficult. The 5/4 was natural for me. But he was married to Abbey Lincoln so when he sent me on

the road to be Abbey Lincoln’s musical director, and that was another good experience. But one night we was in New York and he called me and said, “You know Papa Jo Jones had had an engagement at the Village Gate” and he needed a keyboard player, or a pianist. And Max said, “Would you go to that,” because you know him and Papa Jo were really tight. He said, “I want you to go down there and work with Papa Jo. So you know I’m young, I’m thinking oh shoot, you know, Papa Jones. But actually that was one of the best…
Yeah. Have you ever been in a rhythm section where the bass player and the drummer didn’t seem to be on the same page?
